item.title: An in-universe parody of Are We Cool Yet.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

-Anomalous statue with "Are We Cool Yet" carved into the bottom. Occasionally 'activates', creating a memetic aura causing a variety of effects in people around them. Note attached, filled with nonsensical writing "explaining" the artistic significance of the statue. The effects are assumed by the Foundation to be some kind of pretentious commentary, as most AWCY projects are, and try to figure out what it all means in an attempt to stop its effects or discover its creator.

-Is eventually revealed to be an in-universe parody of AWCY, likely made by a member of ACWY as a sort of self-own after it stops its effects and is reclassified as neutralised.

Central Narrative:

-Foundation attempts to interpret the effects of the statue, researching increasingly obscure art pieces and reaching more and more in an attempt to work out what the artist was trying to say.

-One of the statues effects makes the researchers think the statue is prophesying some catastrophic event, fuelled by their own (justified, at this point) paranoia, and begin kidnapping and interrogating AWCY members to no avail.

-Their interpretations become ridiculously complex in a search for some kind of cohesive meaning, matching the actual effects of the statue becoming more nonsensical and racking up a larger body count in the process. Eventually the statue starts just killing people at random for seemingly no reason, before stopping completely.

-Item is reclassified as "Safe" or "neutralized" and the foundation eventually works out that they have inadvertently been led on a wild goose chase, and deduce the item was meant as a parody of AWCY themselves- meaningless effects resulting in unnecessarily deaths and a note pretentiously explaining the work.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

-The items effects are extremely weird and nonsensical, and the foundation's interpretations of the items effects cross-link other SCP's and reference various societal or historical events, phenomenon, and art pieces.

-As far as I could tell there aren't any AWCY scips that directly make fun of their own group, which seems something right up their alley.

Additional Notes:

-Started as a GAW project, but I prefer it as an actual AWCY member making fun of the group he's apart of.

item.title: Re: A Thousand Door (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Responding to PM request: Sorry if I'm late!
That's an interesting SCP you got there
Would be a shame if someone
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

I hate to be a sore thumb, but unless you make a some major changes, I don't see this as being a successful idea. Your base concept is okay, but its severely lacking in characters, themes, and the general appeal that stories have. What you have right now, at least to me, seems like a glorified mash of a museum and haunted house, which aren't the most original combination. Granted, I'm not exactly into history, which may be why I find the idea so lackluster.

What is SCP trying to prove? That colonialism/slavery/war/etc were terrible and tragic? Most people know that. I feel like you need to take this a step beyond what you currently have. Beyond simple ghosts and demons and classic, cheap horror. You need something real for your audience.

Here's an alternate idea that you can choose to reject/accept:
Each floor of the room causes the participant to physically enter a pocket dimension, where they reenact a scene from the particular era of the floor. For instance, for the 1500s to 1600s, have the person that enters the hall be chased by bloodhounds and and a white man. Maybe have their family running with them, and maybe their son falls behind. The person turns back and attempts to find the son, but sees the dogs have already torn into him. The person turns back and starts running again, and they can hear bullets hitting tree trunks beside their heads, and the thunder of hoofbeats behind them. They try to keep running forward, barefoot and near naked, but they feel a pain in their back, and see blood seeping out of their chest, where they'd been hit by a bullet. The person then falls over, and feels a boot on his head. In front of him, he can see his family still being chased, and he knows they won't make it. He feels a rifle on his head, and with a bang, everything goes black.

When the person wakes up again, they'll find themselves in an empty room with a door. They'll open the door and descend down a flight of stairs, after which they relive another terrifying and tragic scenario. And for added elements of horror, have it so that there's no way to leave. The person can only go forward. They'll be trapped in there, experiencing history forever and ever. And there's not much they can do about it.

Of course you don't need to take that idea, but you need to evoke some sort of emotional response in your audience, especially if you want to make an emotional impact, which is something I feel you want to do.

I'm not going to give this idea a greenlight, at least not yet. But if you go back and refine it, an give some more details, I'll come back and give it a second look. Please PM me with any questions/comments/concerns, and best of luck!


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: A Thousand Door (Seeking Greenlight)

I'll throw a few comments in before this goes away…

— A couple very basic pet peeves:

No SCP should be allowed to wander around the containment site.

When something "appears" to do or be something, the implication is it is/does something completely different and the actual thing should be interesting enough to elaborate on somewhere in the article.

— The "Dr. Wondertainment" aspect doesn't really suit this object and feels tacked on.

— This guy is pretty much a living Mood Ring, which is somewhat amusing but you need to take that somewhere interesting. Since it's a pretty straightforward anomalous effect, maybe the way to go is to give him a good backstory. I was hoping to see that in the interview, but it didn't really add anything. There wasn't a hook on this one to make it at all memorable.

Not gonna lie, I'm digging this idea! A Foundation clone. Or the original foundation that the Foundation was cloned from. who knows? This article is going to be like a dog chasing its tail. Or a tail chasing a dog. It's sure to be a fascinating, mildly infuriating, but nonetheless fun article to see!
You seem to have a solid narrative. Wouldn't it be funny if at the same time SCP was infiltrating the PCS, the PCS was infiltrating the SCP? I kind of like Cybersqyd's idea of having the PCS be an extension of the SCP Foundation and the MTF just raids their own base. Since the two organizations are backronyms of each other, I doubt that such an occurrence could be chalked up to chance. Maybe have some sort of implications or hypotheses to throughout the story? Like the PCS is from an alternate dimension, or both groups are old rivals, or that they're the same organization. Something like that to bring the reader full circle.
I think you have a solid narrative and all. I'm going to just go ahead and give you a tentative greenlight, although I would like you to be a bit more concise with the details. Please feel free to reach out with any questions, and do keep me posted!

item.title: Re: SCP Idea - Security Blanket
item.content:encoded:
Responding to PM
Hey Blackwater!
Interesting SCP you've got here!
It would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

I can certainly see this as a successful SCP, and the concept/narrative of the blanket being the only thing the boy has connecting him to his family is quite intriguing, and potentially emotional. That being said, there are a few places that your story could be tweaked a bit. A lot of them are similar to Red's, and I'd advising re-reading his post to make sure you improve your concept as much as possible.

  • Omnipotence:The blanket does seem to have too much power. For one thing, I'm thinking having the blanket be able to make the boy invisible, invincible, and capable of returning to him a bit much. I'd say scrap one or all of these traits, since they don't seem to be adding much to the story.
  • Mystery: Why are the creatures chasing the blanket? I get the hole mystery of the unknown thing, but I think your story would be a bit more impactful if you gave a reason for why that was happening, and possibly tied it into the backstory of the boy's family
  • Narrative: The anomalous properties of the SCP are important to your article, but the story contained in it is the most important part. Make sure you focus on the emotions, characters, and themes behind your story.
  • Greenlights: From what I can see, you're a first time author. If that's true, I'd say "yes" for seeking greenlights, since you need two to get your concept afloat. I'd definitely be willing to do so if you fixed a couple of things up!

Please keep in mind that this critique isn't meant to bash on you or your writing. It's a great core concept, as far as I'm concerned, and I can definitely see it becoming a popular SCP. It just needs a few tweaks and you're good to go! Please do reach out to me and any other butterfly squad members. After all, we're here to help!

item.title: Re: SCP Idea - Laptop with the ability of abduction
item.content:encoded:
Hi Costansin,

I've read your revised concept on the forums. It's definitely more detailed in terms of the discovery and test logs on the laptop. You've described how the scp works in alot of detail, but we still don't understand why it's doing this and why is it choosing its victims at random. Okay, so they watch a video that's "intriguing" to them? So what? It's goal is simply to get as many victims as possible?

Consider revising the way the laptop picks / chooses its victims, especially since you're going for a mind-affecting anomaly. For example, could it be that the laptop allows a user to chat with a dead loved one from his/her past? This is a more natural way of engaging a user without having to affect his/her mind. An alternative would be for the previous user (now a prisoner in the laptop) to communicate with the new victim in order to trick him/her to take their place. You see where I'm going with this? Your anomalous effects should be connected in some way. Instead, they still seem entirely random.

item.title: Re: Counting Sheep
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there TPE_gaming. Let’s take a look at your concept.

I do see potential here. You’ve crafted an emotional narrative that explains the origins of the scp quite while. I’m also clear about the themes you wish to convey. Before I offer the greenlight, however, I do feel there are a couple of bumps you need to smooth out:

The nine sheep are living embodiments of nine identical music boxes that contain the mental essence of a child that suffered from fatal familial insomnia.

One of my major question marks: why are musical boxes morphing into sheep, and vice-versa. I know you’re trying to go for multiple objects as symbols here, but the more you stretch the reader’s imagination, the harder it is to keep them invested in your world. Why not, for example, just take the musical boxes out of the equation? Have the kid still linked to the sheep in some way (maybe he grew up on a farm, for example) and after his death, his spirit lived on in the animals who were his only companions. Or something like that. I just felt the musical boxes were completely random and unnecessary. But I would also like to hear your thoughts and justification if need be.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll try to take another look. All the best for now!

item.title: Re: The Wild Hunt
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Atomholic. Let's take a look at your concept.

While I applaud your enthusiasm for mythology and desire to bring them to life, there are much better ways to do it besides simply retelling the entire myth word for word. That's what your Central Narrative reads like at the moment: a list of multiple anomalies that happen one after another without additional context or explanation as to their significance.

This does not make for an interesting narrative. Consider SCP-1826, which also involves elements of the mythic Wild Hunt. Notice how they do not simply list the Hunt as a singular event, but weave it into a modern setting, where the Foundation and other characters are also intrinsically involved. You might need to do that here as well. Don't just re-tell a myth as an scp. Instead, find a unique angle / perspective from which to convey elements of the myth.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I'll take another look. Best of luck for now!

item.title: The Price Of Greed
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP

Genre (Optional): Cautionary Tale

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

SCP-XXXX is an old, worn-down wrist watch. It's anomalous effect causes anyone who has seen or heard about the watch, either in person or in some form of media, to seek it out and steal it by any means necessary. Once in possession of the watch an individual will become unnaturally violent and aggressive, especially to others that want to take the watch for themselves.

+ Central Narrative
- Close

The central narrative revolves around the Foundation's difficulty in containing the object because the greed it causes is unending. It begins with the item's initial recovery, where after an incident in which a police officer killed a civilian during a routine traffic stop because he wanted to steal the watch, which the civilian was wearing.

After stealing the watch the officer is beaten to death and the watch is once again stolen. The foundation tracks down this individual due to reports of anomalous activity. During the investigation more casualties occur as the man and two Foundation Officers are killed due to the influence of the SCP-XXXX. After this point, the watch is finally taken into foundation custody.

This series of events would be told through an interview log with the Team Captain and an audio log taken from the police database. Afterward, some test logs will reveal the extent of the watches' influence on people and the kind of powers that it has. An addendum from the site director will issue an order for all records of the watch to be destroyed, and for a mass amnestic to be administered to all personnel assigned to the object due to the extreme effects it has on the human psyche. He will also issue a manhunt for the lead researcher as they have gone AWOL and stolen the watch, leaving more dead in the wake of greed.

+ Hook/Attention-Grabber
- Close

The hook of the story will be that as the article goes on it is revealed that the watch has the secondary effect of causing people who are in possession of the watch to be viewed as a literal monster or something to be threatened by.

For example a foundation agent might view someone wearing the watch as if they looked like SCP-682. This would cause the agent to lash out in fear, possibly killing the watch-bearer, and then steal the watch due to its primary influence. Thus ensuring that the cycle of greed will repeat again.

item.title: Data not redacted?
item.content:encoded:
Something or someone is censoring information on foundation database with ████ or [DATA REDACTED] and it is spreading to all known copies including pyhsical ones.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Classic article with table wizard and dialogs

Elevator Pitch: Basic idea is that something is "corrupting" Foundation database with random censors like ████ or [DATA REDACTED] while the censored information was currently known before and cant be find anywhere including any copies of it. This phenomenon (due to unknown nature SCP-XXXX supposed to be phenomenon for now) is somehow spreading to other articles. You may think that hey maybe thats just normal its some kind of error or GoI spies right? (And no its not, with some logical response. I can explain it if its needed in comments)

Central Narrative: It gives several theories and hypothesis about whats the reason or whats the behind it, is it some sort of entity or GoI spies? Also discovery of it by junior researcher and going to foundation web crawlers one by one to discover it. However this is just a discovery, initial censor that caused by SCP-XXXX might be the source of its spread but it can also not be and might led to much deeper origins.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: So we know that somehow SCP-XXXX corrupts database but how we can be sure that SCP-XXXX didnt corrupt this article. (Lets call it Article A) Answer is simple but effective. If there is any censor in article there must be a explanation for it.

For example: Then solution is [DATA REDACTED] (It has been censored due to being possible cognitohazard.)

So by using this method exclusively for our Article A we can be sure that Article A is not corrupted and safe to read.

item.title: Re: Mr. Bones
item.content:encoded:
I don't think this idea is Greenlight ready yet though I think you could get it there if you keep working on it.

Central Narrative: Mr. Bones is the living skeleton of a deceased European knight who existed during the Crusades, researchers believing him to have taken part in the Fifth Crusade.(1217–1221)
Mr. Bones, at first glance, acts courteous and is willing to partake in interviews and conversations in general without complications. His conversations usually consist of his faith in God and his bone puns, which is repeated on a daily basis.

Seems interesting, I think you could have some fun ideas with this.

Once his War Horn(SCP-XXXX-C) is sounded however, he will immediately become violent, summoning his Sword(SCP-XXXX-A) and Shield(SCP-XXXX-B) from thin air and attack anyone he comes into contact with until the effects wear off or is subdued.

If memories serves it's recommended not to use SCPs that have a 'rage state' in which they go berserk and attack people because it's a bit of a cliche. This also seems to fall into the trap of being a 'thing that kills you' which is an anomaly that doesn't do much interesting beyond killing people.

+ show block
– hide block

So in conclusion this idea feels incomplete maybe? You start with a cool idea about a skeleton blessed with holy power, but than you don't really do anything with it, the story ends up being mostly just a monster who attacks and kills people. You don't tie the idea of him being a crusader into the story except a vague description of him attacking 'unholy' people.

Additional Notes: Their will be several logs will follow interviews with Mr. Bones. This interviews will go in more depth look into the "Berserker state."

The Berserk State is the least interesting idea here (and doesn't link back to the Holy Skeleton concept very well) but it's the part that gets the most focus.

In summery, I really don't think this idea is ready but I would not abandon it entirely, just try reworking it and giving Mr. Bones more stuff to do besides just attacking people.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Mirror Cyborgs
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Science Fiction

Page Layout: Standard SCP article

Elevator Pitch: A pair of cyborgs that appear to be identical and one is trying to assassinate and replace the other. One is just a human with a Gyrfalcon series prosthetic arm, the assassin is an android(Saker, Peregrine, or something in between) with the flesh and blood arm of its target. The human knows nothing of the origin of the android, especially how it got the arm that shouldn't even still be intact. When Anderson Robotics is investigated, even they don't know where the doppelganger came from nor do they have any records of it's construction.

Central Narrative: The android claims to originate from SCP-3560 and implies that all Gyrfalcon prosthetics are actually powered by inhabitants of that dimension which are partially dismantled by Anderson's anomalous construction process. This one regenerated the limb from it's human counterpart and escaped, though how remains a mystery. But it definitely must be contained for futher interrogation and to prevent it from killing it's target. The target has proven to be relatively innocent and agreed to work for the Foundation as a double agent in the Church of Maxwell.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: For every Gyrfalcon, there is a cybernetic doppelganger hunting down the human user, this is just the only one they found so far.

Additional Notes: I'm currently working under the theory that the true power behind Anderson Robotics is the Broken God which has allowed Anderson to build his army, but Anderson has gotten greedy and thinks he can claim the power for himself, and his recent turn of fate is the Broken God getting even with him. SCP-3560 was mentioned to have predated Anderson in a footnote in SCP-4000, I am assuming that rather than simply being an afterlife for the robots, it's more of in between lives, that they existed before and every time Anderson creates a new robot, it's a copy of an existing soul and the all the tech has been reverse engineered from the ancient army of Wan.

item.title: Re: The Hourglass concept
item.content:encoded:
Hi! It seems you're missing the other parts of the template listed here: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13282684/required-reading:how-to-use-this-forum-ideas

Specifically, the Central Narrative, the Hook/Attention Grabber, and the Additional Notes. If these aren't applicable to your concept, just put "None" or something of the sort and you should be fine (though this isn't really recommended as you're probably going to need more than an Elevator Pitch for a greenlight).
^ Don't mind that, lol.

+ Would be kinda rude to just leave that there without crit...
- So I'll give some!

Elevator Pitch: This doesn't feel as creative to me as it could be. The concept of an hourglass that can control time has definitely been thought of before, even if it hasn't been thought of in SCP. Try to think up a creative spin on it, whatever that may be. I do have some nits to pick though.

The thing I'm most confused about is this:

Either the universe will freeze in time upon breakage, or the user that broke the hourglass will have full control over the sands of time.

How do they even figure this out? Are you gonna have some punchline in the article that implies the universe stopping? (Btw, SCP-5510 did it like that with the time-controlling remote so you may wanna think of something different than that)

Also, this:

The user will begin to feel an urge to break the hourglass.

Compulsion effects are generally seen as a cheap way to make your anomaly seem like it has more potential danger. I'd recommend scrapping that, as it feels unnecessary.

Central Narrative: Okay, it causes a universal threat, I read that in your Elevator Pitch. But what's the story? Try to think more about the story you want to tell with your object. An anomaly that could potentially cause reality to fail doesn't really interest me on its own, as it's been done countless times already. Maybe someone stole the hourglass and now they're going on a power trip with it? That's a possible direction you could go in, but try thinking of some more.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Again, a retelling of your Elevator Pitch. Not as important as my crit on the Central Narrative, but still something to think about. What will make it stand out? Universal threats have been done countless times, so think of something that will make your threat stand out from the rest.

Good luck! :)

item.title: Re: Mr. Bones
item.content:encoded:
I think you have a good character here. A super religious skeleton full of bone puns makes for an interesting premise (and I think we always need more light-hearted SCPs on the main site). My main problem is that that’s where you seem to be ending it. You haven’t brought up what you’ll be talking about in the interviews, you haven’t implied that you have any interesting plans for the “berserk mode”, and you’ve actively avoided giving this character any serious backstory.

I also have some more minor critiques: A sword with “kill” written on it seems a little redundant. I’d recommend something like a Bible verse instead. What’s with the war horn? Was it from the crusades? If so, why did they have a horn to make their soldiers go into a mindless rage? Is there a reason he needs to kill in self defense? After all, he is indestructible, so I’d personally find it more interesting if he wouldn’t even fight in self defense and instead just stood there and cracked jokes at the attacker. The same goes for the berserker horn, does he need to fight in defense of it?

Overall, I think this character could lead to an interesting article, but I still want to know what that article is.

item.title: The Hourglass concept
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre : Horror

Elevator Pitch: The Hourglass is right now known as safe, unless its broken. Anomalous effects are given off of the hourglass if physically touched, or around it for a certain amount of time (part inspired by 053). The user will begin to feel an urge to break the hourglass. If the breakage is successful, 2 things have a chance of happening, like a 50/50. Either the universe will freeze in time upon breakage, or the user that broke the hourglass will have full control over the sands of time.

Central Narrative: This concept is to be a unique SCP, it would be safe while docile, but when the hourglass is broken, a universal threat comes into play. While this may not be the best choice, it would seem very interesting as a concept, like the proposal of SCP-001 by S.D Locke.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This concept, once triggered/activated, it will have full control over the universe, either transferring that power to the user that broke the hourglass, or freezing the universe entirely. Even if this were not to happen, it would still be a riot causing devastation within the foundation, and the universe.

Additional Notes: None.

item.title: Re: breath (seeking advice and ideas)
item.content:encoded:
+ only my second critique ever
- never mind

I start out with the disclaimer that I'm new to the site and don't know if this has been done before or not.

I've seen at least one example of a trip into an alternate reality. I'm thinking of SCP-093.

Since it's an SCP article written from the perspective of our reality, there's a physical object that requires containment here while the reality that it allows access to - and the resulting story - takes place in an another dimension.

This raises a fun possibility.

  • SCP team uses anomalous object here in Reality 1 that gives access to a another reality (Reality 2)
  • Team discovers ruins of an SCP Facility in Reality 2 and concludes that their containment of the same object has failed leading to a breach (releasing a virulent parasite) and resulting in this ruined state
  • Through reading the SCP logs of the researchers in Reality 2 they discover that the site was using a system of trial and error to complete containment procedures
  • They realize the the failed containment procedure in Reality 2 is the same procedure that they're using in reality 1. They know that they need to change their procedure but they don't know what the next method to try should be.
  • So, they use the Reality 2 version of the same anomalous object to go to Reality 3 where they find yet another destroyed SCP facility and another failed containment strategy. They learn what failed there.
  • And so on through a series of nested realities until you decide to bring it to resolution.

Story could be told in retrospect through a series of memos. Each from different realities detailing their failure and demise. If you start with memos from the first failed reality and go through to the last you can tell a story of each vain attempt and how the containment becomes more sophisticated over time. Ending with this reality's version of the containment strategy.

As a general note, feedback should ideally be sought before a mainlist post. Readers who vote on articles are not obligated to explain their vote; furthermore, if a piece is negatively rated, reviewers may not be keen to post critique if the page and its discussion thread will be deleted.

The How to Write an SCP Guide has instructions on where/how to seek feedback before posting material to the mainlist.

Forum thread: SCP Announcements 47: Life is like riding a bicycle.

Author, did you happen to follow the feedback-seeking process noted in the How to Write an SCP Guide? There are a lot of immediately noticeable errors, most of which could have been quickly fixed if noted before a mainsite post. For example:

SCP-5978 is a hourglass, standing 9.5 inches tall and has a 6-inch base.

  • Since "hourglass" starts with a vowel sound ("our-glass"), the article used should be "an" and not "a".
  • The Foundation is a scientific organization, and uses metric measurements. Inches are not metric measurements.
  • The parallel structure of "standing […] tall" and "has […] base" is inconsistent.
  • It's not certain what measurement for the base is. Presuming it's got a circular base, the measurement would be specified to the diameter rather than the length of a side.

The rest of the article is similarly in need of edits to maintain the clinical tone that a professional researcher would use. If you haven't looked at the feedback process yet, I highly recommend doing so if you want to submit a successful page to the mainsite.
